paper.title: Data Attribution Should Steer Pretraining
paper.summary: Pretraining data curation decides what a model learns from, yet what makes a document worth learning from depends on what the model already knows. Influence-driven selectors already rank documents to improve one run; we argue that training-data attribution should steer pretraining by identifying testable data properties that become reusable curation criteria, evaluated on new data against cheaper selectors at matched total cost, discovery included. A document ranking is consumed by the run it was computed for, whereas an explained data property can be tested across corpora and checkpoints, especially where familiar quality signals diverge from measured usefulness. Because historical contribution, an understandable explanation, and future data value require distinct evidence, we specify a feedback loop that interprets attributed sources, tests candidate data changes, and states for five claim types what evidence each requires and what none establishes. We close with a falsifiable comparison against perplexity, classifier, and mixing baselines at equal total compute.
paper.comment: Accepted to the 3rd Workshop on Attributing Model Behavior at Scale: Data Attribution and Provenance (ATTRIB 2026) at NeurIPS 2026, Idea Track. 4 pages main text, 13 pages total, 1 figure, 2 tables

analysis.problem_statement: Current pretraining data curation relies on static, run-specific influence rankings that cannot be reused across different corpora or model checkpoints, failing to identify generalizable data properties that predict future utility.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the inefficiency of treating data attribution as a one-off ranking task by proposing a framework that converts attribution signals into reusable, testable data properties. It argues that understanding *why* data is useful allows for cheaper, more scalable curation strategies that can be applied to new datasets without re-computing expensive influence metrics for every new pretraining run.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Comparison of curation effectiveness against baselines at equal total compute

technical_breakdown.method: The paper proposes a feedback loop that interprets attributed sources to identify explainable data properties, which are then tested as reusable curation criteria against cheaper selectors.
technical_breakdown.architecture: A conceptual framework consisting of an attribution interpretation module, a property testing mechanism, and a cost-matched evaluation pipeline.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: The method distinguishes between historical contribution, explanation, and future value, specifying evidence requirements for five distinct claim types to ensure falsifiability.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Aims to reduce computational cost by replacing expensive per-run influence calculations with cheaper, reusable property tests, evaluated at matched total compute including discovery costs.

paper.title: Cache or Denoise Less? Residual Reuse in a Flow-Matching World Action Model
paper.summary: Flow-matching robot policies generate each action chunk through repeated network evaluations, one per denoising step. Cross-cycle caches such as C$^3$ache reuse computation from earlier replanning calls, but whether they beat simply taking fewer steps is unclear. We compare the two in Fast-WAM, a 6B-parameter world action model, on LIBERO-Goal. Two uncached steps keep the success of ten: on all 500 initial states they are non-inferior within two percentage points, for one checkpoint and noise seed. Under PyTorch's default compile mode, they also cut a replanning call on an RTX A6000 from 202 to 92 ms. This leaves little room for caching. A cache that keeps two fresh steps cannot be faster than two uncached steps: every call still encodes the images, runs the video expert and computes those two steps. Caching the first of two steps, refreshed every fourth call, saves at most 11--14% of a call by our cost model. Cached policies are also fragile. Their losses tracked the share of the flow path the cached steps cover: under Fast-WAM's current time shift, C$^3$ache's eight cached steps cover 80% of the path instead of 44%, and the cached policy succeeds on 63% of states against 95% uncached. Resampling the noise on every call cost caches covering 60% or more of the path 14--40 points. These results argue for fewer-step baselines and for testing reuse under the deployed sampler and noise settings. We release our evaluation harness, logs and a checklist.
paper.comment: Honorable Mention at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Efficient Foundation Models for Real-Time Embodied AI (EEAI). Code and data available at https://github.com/gabhinav001/cache-or-denoise-less

analysis.problem_statement: The paper investigates whether cross-cycle caching mechanisms in flow-matching robot policies provide superior latency and performance benefits compared to simply reducing the number of denoising steps.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Inference latency and computational overhead in real-time embodied AI policies using flow-matching models.
analysis.executive_summary: This study challenges the assumption that complex caching strategies like C^3ache are necessary for efficient robot control, demonstrating that reducing denoising steps is often more effective. It reveals that caching can introduce fragility and performance degradation if not aligned with the specific noise schedule and sampler settings. The findings advocate for simpler, fewer-step baselines in the design of real-time world action models.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Latency reduction and task success rate comparison between cached and uncached policies
key_metrics.metric_value: 92 ms (cached/fewer steps) vs 202 ms (baseline); 63% success (cached) vs 95% success (uncached)
key_metrics.baseline: Standard flow-matching policy with 10 denoising steps and C^3ache caching

technical_breakdown.method: Empirical comparison of cross-cycle caching (C^3ache) versus reducing the number of denoising steps in a flow-matching framework, analyzing the impact on latency and success rates under specific noise and time-shift configurations.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Fast-WAM, a 6B-parameter world action model, evaluated on the LIBERO-Goal benchmark.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses PyTorch's default compile mode; analyzes the coverage of the flow path by cached steps (e.g., 80% vs 44%); tests fragility by resampling noise on every call.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Reduces per-call computation by eliminating redundant network evaluations for cached steps, but introduces complexity in managing cache validity and noise consistency.
